published.citation: Rostron et al. 2014, dayside brightness temperature at 4.5 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 2400 +/- 80 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.441.3666R/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 4.5 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 3 measured of 6 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
temperature.facility: Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)
